bio.text: Yoshitoshi's courage, vision and force of character gave ukiyo-e another generation of life, and illuminated it with one last burst of glory.

source.author: John Stevenson
source.title: Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon (1992), quoted in “Tsukioka Yoshitoshi”

bio.text: His career spanned two eras – the last years of Edo period Japan, and the first years of modern Japan following the Meiji Restoration. Like many Japanese, Yoshitoshi was interested in new things from the rest of the world, but over time he became increasingly concerned with the loss of many aspects of traditional Japanese culture, among them traditional woodblock printing.
